perf.summary: Branchless path count avoids a data-dependent branch per node.
perf.currentCost: Per node: nextInPath[i] = match[i]; if (match[i] == -1) numPaths++; — the increment is a data-dependent conditional branch over n nodes, mispredicting on irregular match patterns.
perf.proposedChange: Read int m = match[i] once (avoids two loads of match[i]); set nextInPath[i] = m; accumulate numPaths += (m == -1) ? 1 : 0 (or numPaths -= (m >> 31) style is unsafe for general -1; use the comparison-to-int form which Burst lowers to a branchless setcc add).
perf.rationale: Removes a mispredictable branch and one redundant load of match[i] per iteration, turning the loop into a straight-line accumulate that Burst can vectorize (sum of (m==-1) predicates). Constant-factor but the loop is pure n work.
perf.risk: (m==-1) as int is well-defined and equals the branch's effect. Avoid bit-hacks on the sign bit since only the exact value -1 should count, not all negatives.
